correctness.rationale: The gradient equations force x_i²=s²; no projective solution has x_0=0. In the chart x_0=1 they give exactly the ten listed sign points. The dehomogenized Hessian divided by 6 is diag(epsilon_i)−sJ_4; the rank-one determinant multiplier is 1−s(s−1)=s=±1, so these are nodes. The Segre cubic vanishes there with all first derivatives. An independent rational coefficient computation (python3 /workspace/independent_checks/segre_exact.py) verified the Hilbert vectors of R/(Q,x_0) and R/(Q²+(F),x_0) as (1,4,5) and (1,4,10,19,16); each next graded piece vanishes. Here Q is the ideal of the five displayed quadrics. Lifting bases generates the respective modules over k[x_0] by graded induction, so free modules of ranks 10 and 50 map onto them and onto the actual reduced and doubled point rings. The latter have those ranks after inverting x_0 (ten neighborhoods of length five in the doubled case). The composite maps have torsion kernels inside free modules and therefore zero kernels, proving both unsaturated ideal equalities over every characteristic-zero field. The same exact check gave the degree-four ranks 15 and 20 before and after adjoining the five Fx_i, and all 15 degree-five pairings modulo Q² with nonzero [Fx_0²]. In the shifted quotient algebra R/(I²:F), whose unit corresponds to [F], x_0²=x_1² and each of these squares times the orthogonal hyperplane of its corresponding variable is zero by associativity. The two hyperplanes span degree one by nondegeneracy of B, so every cubic in that quotient vanishes. This proves the Hilbert vector, determinant, socle assertion, and the independent fifteen minimal quartics. The shifted algebra uses multiplication transported via the cyclic generator, not raw multiplication of two representatives in I^{(2)} (which is zero modulo I²). The check used independent finite rational linear algebra, not a replay of the frozen script; it makes no claim in positive characteristic or for higher powers.
